items.followUp: Define the SI unit of work.

rubric.why: Identifies the SI unit of force.
rubric.description: Names the newton as the SI unit of force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating newton or N.

rubric.why: Gives the defining relation for the newton.
rubric.description: One newton produces an acceleration of 1 m/s² in a 1 kg mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct mass and acceleration relation.

modelAnswer: The SI unit of force is the newton (N).
One newton is the force that gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m/s².

rubric.why: States what potential energy is and what it is due to.
rubric.description: Potential energy is stored energy due to an object's position or configuration.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the definition; award 1 mark if energy is identified but its cause is incomplete.

modelAnswer: Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position or configuration.

items.followUp: Write the mathematical equation for mechanical advantage.

rubric.why: Shows the correct ratio of useful output to input and expresses efficiency as a percentage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct output-to-input ratio and 1 mark for multiplying by 100%.

items.followUp: State the two conditions for a body to be in equilibrium.

rubric.description: The resultant force on the body is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the net/resultant force is zero.

rubric.description: The resultant torque (sum of moments) on the body is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the net torque or sum of moments is zero.

modelAnswer: The resultant force acting on the body must be zero.
The resultant torque (sum of moments) acting on the body must be zero.

items.followUp: What is the moment of a force?

rubric.why: States that a couple consists of two equal and opposite forces.
rubric.description: A couple is formed by two equal and opposite forces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the equal-and-opposite force condition.

rubric.why: States the arrangement that makes the forces produce rotation.
rubric.description: The forces act along different parallel lines of action.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the parallel lines of action are separated.

modelAnswer: A couple is formed by two equal and opposite parallel forces.
The forces act along different, separated lines of action.

items.followUp: State the principle of moments for a body in equilibrium.

rubric.why: Identifies the two opposing sets of moments.
rubric.description: The principle compares clockwise and anticlockwise moments about a pivot.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both clockwise and anticlockwise moments.

rubric.why: States the equality required by the principle of moments.
rubric.description: For equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about the same pivot.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating their equality.

modelAnswer: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments about a pivot is equal to the sum of anticlockwise moments about the same pivot.

items.followUp: Define plasma and state two of its properties.

rubric.why: Identifies plasma as an ionized state of matter.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining plasma as ionized/ionised gas.

rubric.why: Gives a characteristic property of plasma.
Provides another characteristic property of plasma.
rubric.description: Plasma is affected by electric or magnetic fields.
rubric.how: This property is included in the definition/property credit; do not exceed 2 marks total.

modelAnswer: It conducts electricity and is affected by electric and magnetic fields.

items.followUp: What is meant by the elastic limit of a material?

rubric.why: Defines deforming force by its effect on a body.
rubric.description: A deforming force is a force that changes a body's shape or size.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the force changes/deforms the body.

rubric.why: Defines elasticity by the body's response when the force is removed.
rubric.description: Elasticity is the property by which a body regains its original shape and size after the deforming force is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating recovery of the original shape or size after removal of the force.

modelAnswer: A deforming force is a force that changes the shape or size of a body.
Elasticity is the property of a body by which it regains its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed.
